title: Dynamic Holdback + Staged Verifier: Optimize Auto-Tuner Postmortem & Recovery Runbook
creator: Aisha Khan
summary: Postmortem of a production regression caused by an aggressive Optimize autotuner change that adjusted batching and KV-cache policies. The incident exposed gaps in staged verification and rollback guardrails. This doc summarizes timeline, root causes, immediate mitigations, and a durable runbook for safe config apply/rollback with a dynamic holdback mechanism.
incident_timeline:
2025-11-02T08:15Z - Optimize autotuner proposed policy set A (aggressive batch increase + longer KV cache TTL)
2025-11-02T08:30Z - Canary apply to 5% traffic in prod region us-west-2 via auto-apply pipeline
2025-11-02T09:02Z - Elevated 95th latency and small spike in token-level rejection errors observed on per-route dashboards
2025-11-02T09:10Z - Alert: route-level latency SLO breach (console alerting). On-call engaged.
2025-11-02T09:18Z - Synced with Optimize team; attempted quick rollback via automated staged-apply API; rollback failed due to stale model-variant compatibility check.
2025-11-02T09:45Z - Engineers manually reverted policy but left behind partial cache entries causing intermittent QoS degradation.
2025-11-02T10:30Z - Full recovery observed after three mitigations and cache invalidation sweep. Post-incident investigation launched.
root_causes: Autotuner generated a policy outside historical stability envelope (batch_size jump + KV-ttl extension) without explicit cost/latency gating.
Canary verification pipeline lacked a shadow-verify step that runs synthetic request sets against the new policy before routing real traffic.
Rollback operation path assumed idempotent cache lifecyle; cache TTL changes left old partial entries causing inconsistent kv cache hits and degraded decoding quality.
Automated rollback failed due to a compatibility check that had a stale mapping for model-variant ids and returned an error without a clear mitigation path for on-call.
Alerting thresholds for Optimize regressions were only token/throughput based; they did not include short-window 95th/99th latency deltas or generation-quality checks tied to prompt testsets.
impact: Approximately 5% of traffic experienced elevated latency and a small number of truncated or malformed responses for 90 minutes in us-west-2. No customer data exposure. Some enterprise customers noticed latency regressions and opened support tickets.
immediate_mitigations_taken: Manual rollback to previous policy by Optimize ops and temporary disable of auto-apply for autotuner changes.
Cache invalidation sweep for impacted hosts, followed by staggered warm-up to avoid cold-start thundering herd.
Increased observability: enabled short-window 1m/5m 95th/99th latency panels and synthetic prompt checks for affected routes.
Contacted three enterprise customers with summary and ETA for follow-up remediation.
Disabled the specific kernel selection path suspected to be sensitive to KV TTL increases for the short term.
decisions_and_rationale:
1) Disable auto-apply for autotuner until staged verifier is implemented: reduces blast radius and gives human review for large delta policies.
2) Introduce a dynamic holdback concept: automatically keep 5-10% of traffic on the incumbent policy as a control cohort during extended canaries to detect regressions in production.
3) Add synthetic shadow verification that runs candidate policies on a reproducible testset (traffic-shaped) and fails apply if quality or latency regress by configured gates.
4) Improve rollback idempotency and add explicit cache lifecycle operations to the apply/rollback API.
Rationale: these changes reduce risk from large configuration deltas while keeping autotuner value by enabling safe progressive rollout and machine-verified checks.
long_term_mitigations: Staged Verifier (MVP): before routing any live traffic, run candidate policy against a synthetic workload in a shadow path and require pass for latency, token-error, and prompt-quality gates.
Dynamic Holdback: for any autotune > X% delta on batch or cache TTL, automatically keep a configurable control cohort (default 7%) on the previous policy for N hours/days.
Rollback API: add explicit 'cache_prune' and 'graceful_wait' parameters to ensure cache-state consistency when TTLs change; document idempotent behavior.
Gating thresholds: add cost/latency delta gates to autotuner and require a scorecard combining 95th latency, token-error-rate, and eval-run quality metrics to pass before apply.
Safety Canary Window: automatic extended monitoring window (e.g., 2x default) for changes that touch KV cache TTL or batching heuristics; keep auto-revert enabled if pass fails.
Alerting: create Optimize-specific runbook alerts that include a short synthetic quality check and route-level 95th delta; route owners subscribed automatically.
Operator UX: console indicators for holdback cohort size, shadow-verifier pass/fail, and a clear one-click hard-revert with cache lifecycle options.
runbook_steps:
1) Triage: on Optimize alert, capture scope (routes, model-variants, regions) and mark incident channel.
2) Quick abort: disable new autotune applies globally via feature-flag 'optimize.auto_apply' if multiple regions affected.
    3) If single-region, set holdback to 100% (route-level) for affected routes to stop propagation.
    4) Attempt automated rollback via /optimize/v1/rollback with 'cache_prune=true' and 'wait_for_warm=false'. If API returns compatibility error, run compatibility-lookup fallback script (scripts/compat-fallback.sh).
    5) If rollback fails, perform manual revert using last-known-good policy id and then run cache-sweep with staggered host groups (group size <= 20% hosts) to avoid thundering herd.
    6) Restore monitoring dashboards and run synthetic prompt quality checks for 30m.
    7) Document the timeline in incident tracker and notify stakeholders.
rollback_checklist: Confirm last-known-good policy id and checksum.
Verify model-variant mapping table is current; refresh from model-registry if stale.
Run compatibility-lookup script prior to calling rollback API to ensure no blocking errors.
Specify cache_prune=true when TTL changes were involved.
If cache_prune is not possible, schedule staggered host invalidation and warm-up with health probes.
Monitor short-window latency and synthetic quality metrics during rollback; keep an escalation path open to SRE lead.
Communicate to support and affected customers with expected timeline.

metrics_and_checks: Baseline: historical 95th latency for route X = 210ms; flag if increase > 20% within 15m window.
Token-error-rate: flag if rate increases > 0.02% absolute or 3x baseline in 10m.
Quality gate: pass if synthetic prompt-set median normalized-ROUGE >= baseline - 2pts.
Cost delta: autotune should not increase per-token cost > 12% without human approval.
retrospective_notes:
The autotuner provides high ROI but needs conservative fallback heuristics when deltas are large.
We should prefer incremental deltas for cache and batching to allow the runtime to adapt without violating QoS.
Human review is not a bottleneck if we make the verifier quick and machine-checkable. Invest in a fast shadow verifier rather than slow manual gates.
Runbooks must include explicit cache semantics; engineers operating rollbacks need simple knobs to prune versus warm-only behavior.
This incident accelerated the roadmap for Optimize guardrails; we estimate shipping the staged verifier and rollback flags within the next cycle will reduce similar incident probability by >75%.
